# claude-jig

> Verify before you code — jig catches spec errors before they become debugging sessions.

jig is a CLI tool for Claude Code that structures the spec → verify → implement cycle. It plugs into Claude Code's lifecycle hooks to provide isolated verification, state tracking across sessions, and completion gates.

## Install

```bash
# Homebrew
brew tap imtemp-dev/tap && brew install jig

# Or one-line install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imtemp-dev/claude-jig/main/install.sh | bash

# Or from source (Go 1.22+)
git clone https://github.com/imtemp-dev/claude-jig.git && cd claude-jig && make install
```

## Initialize

```bash
cd your-project
jig init .
claude   # start Claude Code
```

This deploys skills, hooks, and rules to `.claude/` and creates `.jig/` for state management.

## Recipes

Recipes are structured workflows. Start one inside Claude Code:

```
/jig-spec add OAuth2 authentication
/jig-fix login bcrypt hash comparison fails
/jig-debug session drops after 5 minutes
/jig-design auth system architecture
/jig-map existing codebase
```

| Type | Purpose | Lifecycle |
|------|---------|-----------|
| blueprint | New feature (full spec → code) | discover → scope → research → wireframe → draft ←→ (assess/improve/verify/debate/simulate/audit) → finalize → implement ←→ test → simulate(code) → review → sync → complete |
| fix | Known bug | diagnose → fix-spec → implement ←→ test → complete |
| debug | Unknown bug | 6-perspective analysis → cross-reference → fix-spec → implement ←→ test → complete |
| design | Feature design (spec only) | research → draft ←→ verify → finalize |
| analyze | System understanding (spec only) | research → draft ←→ verify → finalize |

## Phases

Blueprint phases in order:
`discovery` → `scoping` → `research` → `wireframe` → `draft` → `assess` → `improve` → `verify` → `debate` → `simulate` → `audit` → `finalize` → `implement` → `test` → `review` → `sync` → `status` → `complete`

Implementation phases (shared across blueprint, fix, debug):
`implement` → `test` → `simulate`(code) → `review` → `sync` → `status` → `complete`

## File Structure

```
.jig/
├── config/              # git tracked — settings, template version
│   ├── settings.yaml
│   └── .template-version
├── specs/               # git tracked — recipe specs, project docs
│   ├── vision.md
│   ├── roadmap.md
│   ├── project-status.md
│   ├── project-map.md
│   ├── debates/{id}/        # project-level debates (meta.json + rounds)
│   └── recipes/{id}/
│       ├── recipe.json         # recipe state (id, type, topic, phase)
│       ├── intent.md           # discovery output
│       ├── scope.md            # scoping output
│       ├── wireframe.md        # structure design
│       ├── draft.md            # working spec
│       ├── final.md            # finalized spec (Level 3)
│       ├── manifest.json       # document relationships
│       ├── changelog.jsonl     # action log
│       ├── verify-log.jsonl    # verification history
│       ├── tasks.json          # implementation tasks
│       ├── test-results.json   # test results
│       ├── deviation.md        # spec-code differences
│       ├── review.md           # code review findings
│       ├── diagnosis.md        # fix/debug: root cause
│       ├── fix-spec.md         # fix/debug: change spec
│       ├── debates/{id}/       # recipe-level debates
│       └── simulations/        # simulation results
└── local/               # gitignored — runtime data
    ├── metrics.jsonl
    ├── work-state.json
    └── recipes/{id}/metrics.jsonl
```

## CLI Reference

```
jig                         Active recipe status
jig init [dir]              Initialize project
jig doctor [recipe-id]      Health check
jig ls                      List recipes                      (= jig recipe list)
jig new --topic <topic>     Create a recipe                   (= jig recipe create)
jig log <id>                Record action / phase             (= jig recipe log)
jig ask [recipe-id]         Hold a question only you can answer  (= jig recipe decision hold)
jig ans <id> <key>          Answer a held question            (= jig recipe decision resolve)
jig stats [recipe-id]       Metrics and cost (--json, --csv)
jig graph [recipe-id]       Document relationship graph
jig verify <file>           Check document consistency
jig validate [recipe-id]    JSON schema check
jig sync-check [recipe-id]  Verify document sync
jig update                  Update templates
jig version                 Show versions
```

## Skills (21)

Inside Claude Code, invoke skills with `/skill-name`:

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| /jig-spec | Full spec-to-code lifecycle |
| /jig-design | Design spec (Level 2) |
| /jig-map | Analysis spec (Level 1) |
| /jig-fix | Bug fix with diagnosis |
| /jig-debug | Multi-perspective debugging |
| /jig-discover | Intent discovery conversation |
| /jig-wireframe | Structure design with mermaid diagrams |
| /jig-research | Codebase and external research |
| /jig-verify | Logical verification (fork context) |
| /jig-cross-check | Internal consistency check (fork context) |
| /jig-audit | Completeness audit (fork context) |
| /jig-assess | Level assessment and next-action decision |
| /jig-sync-check | Document synchronization check (fork context) |
| /jig-debate | Structured 3-expert debate |
| /jig-adjudicate | Evaluate debate conclusions |
| /jig-simulate | Scenario walkthrough — document or code (fork context) |
| /jig-implement | Code generation from finalized spec |
| /jig-test | Test generation and execution |
| /jig-review | Multi-perspective code review (fork context, 3 parallel agents) |
| /jig-sync | Sync spec with implementation |
| /jig-status | Project status aggregation |

## Models

Main session model handles all primary work and core quality gates.

Fork context agents run in separate AI instances (no shared conversation history).
Core gates use session model for maximum quality. Pattern-based checks use sonnet.

| Agent | Default | Setting |
|-------|---------|---------|
| verifier | session model | agents.verifier |
| auditor | session model | agents.auditor |
| simulator | session model | agents.simulator |
| reviewer_quality | session model | agents.reviewer_quality |
| reviewer_security | sonnet | agents.reviewer_security |
| reviewer_arch | session model | agents.reviewer_arch |
| reviewer_validator | sonnet | agents.reviewer_validator |
| reviewer_rebuttal | session model | agents.reviewer_rebuttal |
| simulator_validator | sonnet | agents.simulator_validator |
| simulator_rebuttal | session model | agents.simulator_rebuttal |
| diagnosis_validator | session model | agents.diagnosis_validator |
| diagnosis_rebuttal | session model | agents.diagnosis_rebuttal |

Override in `.jig/config/settings.yaml`. Options: sonnet, opus, haiku.

## Completion Gates

Specs complete when: verification.md exists, verify-log last entry shows critical=0 major=0. Output `<jig>DONE</jig>`. This sets phase to `finalize`.

Implementation completes when: all tasks done, tests pass, review.md exists, deviation.md exists. Output `<jig>IMPLEMENT DONE</jig>`.

Fix completes when: fix-spec.md exists, tests pass. Output `<jig>FIX DONE</jig>`.

## Key Rules

1. Every document modification triggers /jig-verify immediately after.
2. Verification runs in separate agent context (never self-review).
3. Edit draft.md in place (Edit tool), don't rewrite.
4. Log every action: `jig recipe log {id} --action [type] --output [path]`.
5. Run /jig-simulate at least once before Level 3.
6. Run /jig-adjudicate after every debate.
7. Run /jig-sync-check before finalizing.
8. Deviations are reports, not gates — they don't block completion.

## Document Levels

- Level 1 (Understanding): components listed, relationships explained, tech stack specified
- Level 2 (Design): data flow, error handling, interfaces, rationale for choices
- Level 3 (Implementation-ready): every file path, function signature, type, edge case, test scenario specified

jig version: 0.2.0
